name: Common (and deep/superficial) peroneal nerve
summary: The smaller lateral division of the sciatic nerve (L4–S2) runs along the medial border of biceps femoris to the lateral side of the popliteal fossa, winds around the neck of the fibula (where it lies on bone under thin skin) and divides into the deep peroneal nerve, which supplies the anterior compartment (tibialis anterior, extensor digitorum longus, extensor hallucis longus) and the first web space skin, and the superficial peroneal nerve, which supplies the evertors (peroneus longus and brevis) and the dorsum of the foot. Compression at the fibular neck by crossed legs, casts, weight loss or squatting is the commonest cause of foot drop.

anatomy.location: Lateral popliteal fossa along the tendon of biceps femoris, around the neck of the fibula deep to peroneus longus (the fibular tunnel), where it divides; the deep branch runs on the interosseous membrane with the anterior tibial artery, the superficial branch in the lateral compartment.

subdivisions.name: Common peroneal nerve
subdivisions.note: short head of biceps femoris (in the thigh, from the sciatic trunk), lateral sural cutaneous nerve

subdivisions.name: Deep peroneal nerve
subdivisions.note: tibialis anterior, extensor digitorum longus and brevis, extensor hallucis longus, peroneus tertius; first dorsal web space

subdivisions.name: Superficial peroneal nerve
subdivisions.note: peroneus longus and brevis (eversion); dorsum of the foot and lateral leg

function: Ankle dorsiflexion and toe extension (deep), foot eversion (superficial), and sensation of the dorsum of the foot and the lateral leg.

bestView.label: cervical cord; the peroneal nerve derives from L4–S2

imaging.normalAppearance: Peripheral nerves of the limbs are outside the MNI brain volume; no atlas mesh is shown. Ultrasound and MR neurography image the nerve directly; electrodiagnosis localizes the lesion functionally. Ultrasound and MRI at the fibular neck show nerve swelling, an intraneural ganglion from the tibiofibular joint, or a fibular head fracture, with denervation of the anterior and lateral compartments.

pathology.pathology: Peroneal neuropathy at the fibular neck
pathology.finding: Enlarged nerve at the fibular neck; nerve conduction shows conduction block across the fibular head.
Cystic expansion of the nerve tracking from the superior tibiofibular joint.
Swollen anterior compartment muscles with deep peroneal nerve involvement after trauma or exertion.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Nerve conduction across the fibular neck; EMG including short head of biceps femoris; ultrasound

lesionEffects.deficit: Foot drop with weak eversion, steppage gait, numbness of the dorsum of the foot
lesionEffects.mechanism: Common peroneal nerve at the fibular neck

lesionEffects.deficit: Foot drop with preserved eversion and numbness limited to the first web space
Weak eversion with dorsal foot numbness and normal dorsiflexion

lesionEffects.mechanism: Tibial nerve and S1 intact, distinguishing it from sciatic and L5 lesions

examination: Dorsiflexion, toe extension and eversion against resistance; inversion (should be normal)
Sensation of the dorsum, first web space and lateral leg
Tinel at the fibular neck; look for a habit of crossing the legs, recent weight loss or a cast
pearls: Foot drop with normal inversion is peroneal; with weak inversion it is L5 or sciatic
Weight loss plus foot drop: the nerve has lost its fat cushion at the fibular neck
